title: SCHEMES FOR TRIBALS IN WEST BENGAL
body_text:
Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed today in Lok Sabha that the details of progress of interventions under PM JANMAN in the State of West Bengal (as on 30.06.2026), based on the information provided by the concerned Ministries/Department, is as under:

MoP (RDSS) MNRE MoC (DoT-USOF) MoTA HHs Sanctioned HHs Electrified HHs Sanctioned HHs Electrified Habitation planned for coverage Habitation covered MPCs sanctioned MPCs completed VDVKs sanctioned Business Started 3372 3372 - - 12 3 - - 5 -
The details of progress of interventions under PM JANMAN in Purulia District , West Bengal (as on 30.06.2026), based on the information provided by the concerned Ministries/Department, is as under:
Name of the District Purulia MoJS No of Villages Sanctioned 5 No of Villages Saturated 0 MoHFW MMUs sanctioned & Operational 3 MoTA No of VDVKs sanctioned 1 No of VDVKs business started 0
Under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JGUA), during the current financial year, Ministry has also approved projects amounting to Rs.12574.70 lakhs
in State of West Bengal for MoTA components under the abhiyan. In respect of Purulia district. approvals have been accorded for:
Construction of 204 Additional Classrooms amounting to Rs 2,417.3 lakh; 1 Hostel Repair/Renovation work amounting to Rs 39.99 lakh; and 1 Tribal Multi-Purpose Marketing Centre (TMMC) amounting to Rs 100 lakh.
State Government had undertaken habitation level data collection exercise through PM Gati Shakti mobile application to estimate PVTG population figures and infrastructure gaps in order to cover PVTG population residing in villages & habitations under PM JANMAN. The details of number of PVTG habitations identified (tentative) and PVTG population in the State of West Bengal is tabulated below:
No. of District No. of Blocks No. of Villages No. of PVTG habitations PVTG HHs PVTG Population 4 24 428 495 19991 68720
Ministry has been regularly taking up the issue of implementation of activities under PM JANMAN with State Government of West Bengal.
Besides, PVTG household survey is also ongoing in State of West Bengal and State Government has surveyed 18173 PVTG households. The State Government is required to examine the data captured and take appropriate action in consultation with line Departments to address the gaps identified in terms of schemes norms and eligibility criteria.
The responsibility of allocation and release of funds to districts is the responsibility of State Government. Hence, the records of funds allocated, released and utilized, district-wise, is maintained by the State Government.
The formulation and submission of proposals is the responsibility of State Government and District Administration. State Government had not submitted any proposals for MPCs including in Purulia District to Ministry of Tribal Affairs. However, Ministry of Tribal Affairs has carried out an orientation programme on schemes of MoTA including PM JANMAN and DA JGUA for Officers of State Governments to facilitate formulation of proposals and progress thereon.

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey gave a status update on PM JANMAN scheme implementation in West Bengal as of 30 June 2026, including progress on housing, roads, water, health, nutrition, education, electrification and mobile connectivity for tribal households, with specific data for Purulia district. He also noted that Rs.12,574.70 lakh has been approved under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JGUA) for West Bengal, and that West Bengal has identified 495 PVTG habitations with a PVTG population of 68,720 across 4 districts and 24 blocks.
enrichment.context:
PM JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), launched in November 2023, is a Rs.24,000 crore mission to provide basic infrastructure and services—housing, roads, water, health, nutrition, education, electricity, and telecom connectivity—to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) through convergence of 11 ministries. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JGUA), launched later, aims at saturating development in tribal-majority villages beyond just PVTGs, covering aspects like classrooms, hostels, and Tribal Multi-Purpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs) to boost livelihoods.

This reply highlights the federal division of implementation responsibility: while the Centre approves and funds central components, the actual formulation of proposals, and fund allocation/release to districts, rests with the State Government. The response points to gaps in West Bengal's implementation—such as no MPC (Multi-Purpose Centre) proposals being submitted from the state, and only partial saturation of villages under JJM despite houses under PMAY-G and PMGSY showing zero sanctioned units in the state as per data given—reflecting recurring center-state coordination challenges in scheme delivery.

prelims_questions.question: The 'PM JANMAN' scheme is primarily aimed at the welfare and development of which of the following groups?
prelims_questions.explanation: PM JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan) is specifically designed to provide basic infrastructure and services to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

prelims_questions.question: Under PM JANMAN, which of the following is NOT one of the components covered through ministry convergence as mentioned in official implementation reports?
options: Universal basic income for tribal households
Piped water supply under Jal Jeevan Mission
prelims_questions.explanation: PM JANMAN converges housing (PMAY-G), roads (PMGSY), water (JJM), health, nutrition, education, electrification and telecom, but does not include a universal basic income component.

mains_questions.question: PM JANMAN represents a convergence-based model for tribal welfare involving multiple central ministries. Discuss the challenges of implementing such multi-ministerial schemes at the state and district level, with reference to the division of responsibilities between the Centre and State Governments.

Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) continue to lag behind in human development indicators despite decades of targeted schemes. Critically examine the reasons for this persistent gap and suggest measures for more effective last-mile delivery of welfare programmes to PVTGs.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 1 - Indian Society / GS Paper 2 - Governance
